arms.predicted: Formula achieves <=78% accuracy (<=14/18 correct). All 4+ failures involve qwen3-32b or L40S qwen3-14b. Formula predicts TP=4 where TP=8 actually wins due to model-size blindness.
arms.observed: Formula achieves 83.3% accuracy (15/18 correct). 3 failures (not 4+): (1) A100-SXM qwen3-32b rate=500: formula predicts TP=4 (500>196), actual TP=8, score=0.101861 vs global_best=0.108182 (5.8% below). (2) L40S qwen3-14b rate=500: formula predicts TP=4 (500>463), actual TP=8, score=0.080647 vs global_best=0.084795 (4.9% below). (3) L40S qwen3-32b rate=500: formula predicts TP=4 (500>463), actual TP=8, score=0.056742 vs global_best=0.064436 (11.9% below). Notably: H100 qwen3-32b rate=500 is CORRECT because TP=4 actually wins at rate=500 (crossover ~350, rate=500>crossover), so formula accidentally predicts right. Formula achieves 15/18, not <=14/18 as predicted. All 15 correct predictions match exactly or within 0.7% of global best. The 3 failures all involve TP=4 prediction where TP=8 dominates: A100-SXM 32B (no crossover at all rates), L40S 14B (no crossover), L40S 32B (no crossover).
arms.diagnostic_note: The direction is confirmed (formula does fail, failures involve 32B models and L40S), but the magnitude is wrong: 3 failures instead of 4+ predicted, giving 83.3% accuracy instead of <=78%. The discrepancy arises because H100 qwen3-32b rate=500 is a 'lucky' correct prediction: the formula predicts TP=4 because 500>119 (formula crossover), and TP=4 actually IS the winner at rate=500 for qwen3-32b on H100 (true crossover ~350). The test matrix rates of 100 and 500 happen to land on opposite sides of both the formula crossover AND the true crossover for this regime. Testing at intermediate rates (200-400) would expose the H100 32B formula failure, as predicted by the designer handoff. The mechanism is confirmed: formula is model-size-blind (uses only bandwidth), causing failures for 32B models on lower-bandwidth hardware where the crossover is pushed above practical rates.

arms.diagnostic_note: Perfect 4/4 prediction confirmed. The TP=8 win margin at 100 requests is surprisingly large (16-38%), indicating the queuing advantage of 2 instances is not just absent but actively reversed at short horizons. At 100 requests, TP=8/1inst's inherently lower per-step latency completely dominates over TP=4/2inst's load-distribution advantage. The minimum evaluation horizon for reliable TP winner identification at high rates is >500 requests (as established in iter-7 probes) and empirically at least 1000 requests.
